title: Dual-metric-axis accessible labels derive the secondary series from raw data order, not the color-scale domain

complexity.rationale: The correct source (the live color-scale domain) isn't available where the nav structure is built, so a robust fix needs either a shared spec-builder helper or reading the resolved domain from the Vega view — a design decision, though the code change itself is small.

summary: For a dual-metric-axis bar with accessibleNavigation, the per-series metric axis title is chosen by treating the last distinct color value in raw data order as the secondary-axis series. The spec builder instead assigns the secondary axis to peek(domain(COLOR_SCALE)). These match for a default ordinal color scale but diverge under a custom color-scale sort/explicit domain or a hidden series, causing a leaf to announce the wrong metric axis.
symptom: With accessibleNavigation on a dual-metric-axis bar whose color scale is sorted/filtered (or has a hidden series), a focused bar can announce the wrong metric axis title (e.g. a bar plotted against the primary axis is read with the secondary axis's title, or vice versa).
rootCause: navMetricTitleBySeries in packages/react-spectrum-charts-s2/src/RscChart.tsx computes the secondary-axis series as the last element of the distinct color values in raw `data` first-appearance order. The spec builder's source of truth is the LAST_RSC_SERIES_ID signal, updated to peek(domain(COLOR_SCALE)) — the last element of the resolved color-scale domain (packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/signal/signalSpecBuilder.ts, getLastRscSeriesIdSignal), which addDualMetricAxisData uses to split rows onto the primary vs secondary axis (packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/bar/barSpecBuilder.ts, addDualMetricAxisData). Raw data order and the color-scale domain order are different sources: they coincide only for a default ordinal domain with no sort and no hidden series. The nav structure is built once at attach time (packages/react-spectrum-charts-s2/src/dataNavigator/dataNavigatorAdapter.ts) before the Vega view is guaranteed to exist, so RscChart cannot currently read the resolved domain and replicates the ordering from the raw data prop instead.

comparison.aspect: Which series is the secondary-axis series
comparison.expected: peek(domain(COLOR_SCALE)) — the last series in the resolved color-scale domain (respects sort/explicit domain and excludes hidden series).
comparison.actual: The last distinct color value in raw data first-appearance order, ignoring any color-scale sort/domain and still including hidden series.

crossCutting.notes: requiresS1S2Parity: false — accessibleNavigation/dataNavigator exists only in the s2 packages. A robust fix may need to read the resolved color-scale domain from the live Vega view (or a shared helper exported from vega-spec-builder-s2) rather than recomputing series order in the React layer.

implementationPlan.change: Bug location (navMetricTitleBySeries): picks the secondary series from raw data order. Fix direction: derive it from the resolved color-scale domain instead — e.g. read domain(COLOR_SCALE) from the live Vega view once available (and rebuild/refresh labels), or at minimum exclude hiddenSeries and honor any color sort so it matches the spec builder.
Reference (getLastRscSeriesIdSignal): defines the secondary-series source of truth (peek(domain(COLOR_SCALE))) the nav must match.
Reference (addDualMetricAxisData): splits rows onto primary/secondary axes by SERIES_ID vs LAST_RSC_SERIES_ID — confirms which series belongs to which axis.

openQuestions: Is reading the resolved domain from the live Vega view feasible without rebuilding the nav structure (which is intentionally built once to preserve focus), or should vega-spec-builder-s2 expose a shared series-ordering helper the React layer can call synchronously?
Beyond a custom color sort, does hidden-series filtering already reproduce this divergence with existing props, making it more than theoretical?
